scope: Systematic review of the diagnosis of drug-induced interstitial lung disease, including how often biopsy agrees with the clinical diagnosis.

keyRecommendations.text: A study of transbronchial biopsy or BAL reported overall diagnostic agreement of 67% with the clinical diagnosis of drug-induced ILD.
A single-centre series of transbronchial or open biopsy reported lower diagnostic agreement (45%).

clinicalBottomLine: Drug-induced ILD is a clinical diagnosis. Biopsy and lavage do not always agree with that diagnosis; one cited series found 67% agreement and another 45%.
notableCaveats: The review is about diagnostic agreement, not a drug-by-drug dose table.

source.title: Drug-Induced Interstitial Lung Disease: A Systematic Review.
